text: The old lighthouse keeper swore the wind remembered every name ever whispered across the bay carrying them back when storms arrived thick and restless He kept a notebook of voices he thought he heard on nights when fog swallowed the light entirely Some were familiar his brother's laugh his mother's lullaby Others were strangers speaking languages he never learned yet somehow understood No one believed him of course People smiled politely and called it loneliness the way isolation invents company But on my last visit I stayed until midnight and heard it too Not words exactly but pressure behind words like a hand pressed against wet glass The air vibrated with unspoken apologies unfinished arguments promises made to children who never came back The keeper looked at me and nodded as if to say you see I told you so We sat in silence afterward listening to rain hit tin roof and thinking about how much human sound must still linger in atmosphere even after sources are gone Radio waves laughter distress signals perhaps never truly vanish they just thin until only certain ears can perceive them Maybe memory is not inside us at all Maybe we are inside memory vast and collective and patient I left before dawn but the wind followed me inland for miles humming something I almost recognized When I finally slept I dreamed of water that glowed without light and voices that glowed without sound waiting quietly to be heard again by anyone willing to listen
